g1.label: 1. I am writing ___ the internship…
g1.why: Write about + a topic to say what the email is about.

g2.label: 2. Could you ___ me some information…
g2.why: We give information. We do not say say me or explain me.

g3.label: 3. I was wondering ___ it is possible…
g3.why: Whether introduces an indirect question after wondering.

g4.label: 4. Would you mind ___ me the form?
g4.why: After would you mind, use the -ing form.

g5.label: 5. Thank you for your ___.
g5.why: After your, use the noun help.

g6.correct: Could you tell me how to cancel my membership?
accept: Could you tell me how to cancel my membership?
g6.label: 6. To a gym manager
g6.why: It is a polite question. The others are an order and a legal-sounding demand.

g7.correct: I was wondering if it would be possible to move my exam to a later date.
accept: I was wondering if it would be possible to move my exam to a later date.
g7.label: 7. To the exam office
g7.why: It is polite and clear. The others are an order and far too stiff.

g8.correct: Would it be possible to extend the loan of this book?
accept: Would it be possible to extend the loan of this book?
g8.label: 8. To the library
g8.why: Would it be possible to… is a polite request. The others are blunt or stiff.

g9.correct: I am writing to ask whether you have a room available in March.
accept: I am writing to ask whether you have a room available in March.
g9.label: 9. The first line of an email to a landlord
g9.why: It gives the reason neutrally. The others are slang and over-formal.

g10.label: 10. Thank you ___ your quick reply.
g10.why: The fixed phrase is thank you for + noun.
